questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go north and not travel very far with planes. Exploring culture of nearby countries.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: KI has a website and it was easy to find arrival information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt need any

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy because it was through the university. Otherwise you can look at "SSSB" in Stockholm

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived just 10 minutes on bike from campus, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room and kitchen was functional but not very nice. I lived close to water and nature, shopping and the metro which was very nice though

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply through KI website and through a mobility online from Katolinska Institutet.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: KI-website is good and the international coordinator is very kind and helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The 8-weeks gyn/obs-course is very nice because it follows sweedish students and you have classes and not just clinics. Follow this with the pediatrics course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's very similar to Denmark

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar to Denmark. We had to do individual projects as well on topics that we chose ourselves. This was different.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Volleyball mostly. Hikes. Museums.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I like playing volleyball, and I did so at KI and a club called SSIF. It was nice if you like volleyball.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and see museums - Sweden are good at incorporating arts and science i think. Take the ferry out to Skærgården and go for some nice hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy because it is similar. I think it's very nice to be a dane in Sweden. As soon as you show a little interest in Sweden and their culture, they are very very kind to you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to a lot of the activities that the university is planning - there's a lot of them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I talked swedish all the time, which i guess was a bit hard in the start, but very rewarding in the end.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kanelbuller, "Lagom", they are very inclusive in Sweden and appreciate students as well. It's really very nice and cozy being in Sweden and very nice to get to know our neighbours better!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do it! It's very nice to be a Dane in Sweden and there's so much nice culture and nature that you can uncover! And it's very nice getting to know our neighbours better! You don't have to travel to exotic lands far away and put strain on the climate to expand your perspective.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can take "Snälltåget" to Stockholm, which is very cheap and then you get a plus on your erasmus green-grant

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and swedish culture. Getting a nice relation to a country nearby.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living alone in a dorm room that was not very social. Having to organize everything yourself

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nop

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
